correctness.rationale: The DCT-I orthogonality identity with endpoint weights w0=wN=v0=vN=1/2 gives full (N+1) orthogonal Q. Two-row/two-last-column block partition identifies the N−3 unit singular squares of the surviving (N−1)×(N−1) matrix and the two eigenvalues of BᵀB. The deleted-row block has vectors (−1)^j√(2w_j/N)(x_j,1/√2), yielding trace 2t/N and determinant 2w_jw_l(x_j−x_l)²/N² and positive eigenvalues for distinct nodes. Lower bound μ−≥2w_jw_lΔ²/[3N(w_j+w_l)] for every pair, combined with Rayleigh upper bound μ−_{0,1}≤2δ²/(3N), and cosine-grid spacing (>2δ between interiors, >3δ non-nearest endpoints, Δ=2 between endpoints), strictly rules out every erasure except endpoint neighbors. Reflection ties two patterns. Exact formula α=(t−√(t²−δ²))/N with t=5/4+c², δ=1−c yields α~π⁴/(18N⁵), κ=1/α~18N⁵/π⁴. Independent SVD and formula agree for all erased pairs at N=4,5,8,16,32 and locate same optimizers; tests are finite corroboration, proof all N analytical.

value.rationale: Sharp loss-of-two-data stability for a natural quadrature-orthogonal interpolation grid identifies the unique bad missing-node geometry and the exact polynomial blowup of energy conditioning. This complements, rather than renames, known single deletion Lebesgue growth and near-Nyquist half-shifted cosine results; researchers assessing erasure resilience could need the precise DCT-I weighted constants.

final_claim: For each N≥4, deleting any two rows and retaining degrees 0..N−2 of the orthonormal DCT-I matrix yields an invertible square sampler. Nonunit squared singular values are [t±√(t²−2w_jw_l(x_j−x_l)²)]/N, and unique worst erasures up to reflection are {0,1}, {N−1,N}. Their least squared singular value ~π⁴/(18N⁵) and worst squared condition ratio ~18N⁵/π⁴.
limitations: N≥4 weighted orthonormal DCT-I and exactly two known erasures; no unweighted/unknown erasure/noisy-node claim.
